Package org.geysermc.paletter.block

Class CustomBlock

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.block.CustomBlock
public final class CustomBlock extends Object
A custom (data driven) block: an add-on JSON minecraft:block in Java. Registering one in a layer generates its states, its block property data, its block item and its creative entry; runtime ids and palette ordering are handled by the palette. 

 CustomBlock lamp = CustomBlock.builder("example:lamp")
     .property(BlockProperty.bool("example:lit"))
     .trait(PlacementDirection.builder().enabledStates(PlacementDirection.EnabledStates.CARDINAL_DIRECTION).build())
     .component(Geometry.of("minecraft:geometry.full_block"))
     .component(MaterialInstances.builder().all(MaterialInstances.Instance.builder().texture("lamp").build()).build())
     .permutation("q.block_state('example:lit')", LightEmission.of(15))
     .creative(CreativePlacement.loose(CreativeCategory.CONSTRUCTION))
     .build();

An instance owns its type() (with its states) and its itemType(): the palette hands back exactly those for the block, so they can be compared with ==. Equal blocks (same identifier and definition) are equals, but each has types of its own, see type().

Since:
1.0.0

    • type

      public @NonNull BedrockBlockType type()
      The type of the block, to use it like a vanilla BedrockBlocks constant. Its states have canonical ids per layer lineage, see Palette.runtimeId(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState).

      It is created with the block and belongs to it: every call returns the same type with the same states, and a palette the block is registered in hands back exactly these for it (block, decode, Palette#blockState, ...), so == works like for vanilla constants. Another, equal block has a type of its own, equal to this one but not identical: a palette hands back the type of the instance its layer registered.

      Returns:
      the type of the block
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • itemType

      public @NonNull BedrockItemType itemType()
      The type of the block item, owned by the block like type(): a palette hands back this type and its base variant for the block item. A palette has the item if it is registered: with the block unless item() is CustomBlock.BlockItem.NONE, or by a later layer (PaletteLayer.Builder.blockItem(java.lang.String, org.geysermc.paletter.block.CustomBlock.BlockItem, org.geysermc.paletter.creative.CreativePlacement)).
      Returns:
      the type of the block item
      Since:
      1.0.0
